races.title: State Senate, District 22
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: LaKeshia M. Alston
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 22 (Durham). Durham native and educator who says she worked 11 years for Durham Public Schools. She also says she started small businesses in the aesthetics field. Holds a bachelor's degree from Winston-Salem State University. No elected office on record.
cands.gaps: We found no voting record, bills, or official filings from Alston, because she has not held office. We found no stated position from her on data centers, homestead tax elimination, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. Her stated priorities are unionizing teachers, FDA-style manufacturing filters and field offices, commercial property tax changes, tax benefits for home ownership, intellectual property protection for university students, affordable health insurance and housing, and AI technology. None of these maps clearly onto those topics. We could not independently confirm her work history, business ventures, or education beyond her Winston-Salem State University bachelor's degree and Aveda associate's degree listed on Ballotpedia. Her campaign site's claims about Grand Canyon University and Wake Tech are unconfirmed. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her. No news coverage or controversies turned up.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign site calls her a native of Durham who grew up in the city, and her Ballotpedia survey response calls her a Durham native.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: She says she spent eleven years with Durham Public Schools as a substitute, interventionist, teaching assistant and classroom teacher. She also says she started small businesses after earning an esthetics credential from Aveda in 2020. She has not held elected office.
qual.why: She has no legislative, policy or budget record and no elected office. Her work is mainly teaching and small-business activity, which is only loosely related to writing law and budgets. The business details come from her own site and are vague.

cands.name: Sophia Chitlik
cands.bio: Democrat who has served in the North Carolina Senate for District 22 (Durham) since January 2025, after defeating incumbent Mike Woodard in the 2024 primary. Former Obama campaign organizer, U.S. Department of Labor and White House staffer, nonprofit chief operating officer, consultant and investor.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina endorsed her in 2026, along with several voter-guide groups listed on Ballotpedia.

Her 2026 campaign site lists endorsements from Durham-area officials, including State Sen. Natalie Murdock, Reps. Zack Hawkins, Marcia Morey, Vernetta Alston and Ray Jeffers, Sens. Mujtaba Mohammed, Caleb Theodros and DeAndrea Salvador, and former Mayor Steve Schewel.
In 2024 she listed endorsements from the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People, the Durham People's Alliance and the Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, only that she was raised in Burbank, California; her birth year is given only as 1989 or 1990. We found no documented actions or statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or school vouchers. Her campaign site lists over 100 sponsored bills, but the pages we had did not name specific bills on these topics. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her stated positions come only from her campaign platform and a 2024 survey. Her stated housing position, to expand affordable housing and change zoning laws, was not matched to any topic because it did not clearly fit.

local.label: Roots 20: Wikipedia says she was raised in Burbank, California and has lived in Durham since 2017, which is under 10 years in North Carolina as an adult.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Sitting NC state senator since 2025. Earlier she worked in the U.S. Department of Labor and the White House, was chief operating officer of The Future Project (an $11 million-budget education nonprofit), and worked as a strategic planning consultant and investor.
qual.why: She has legislative service as a senator, plus federal government and policy work and senior management experience. Her committee seats and fellowships were not counted.
